commitResults.messageBody: Move scanner ownership, prompts, separators, and Rem-prefixed output into a dedicated Ui class. This gives the main command loop a single boundary for user interaction and prepares it for further decomposition without changing the tested console behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add UI class and implement it

commitResults.messageBody: Move command recognition, argument validation, and task construction out of Rem. Keeping parsing rules together gives the command loop a narrower orchestration role and creates a clear boundary for the remaining TaskList extraction.

Introduce TaskList as the owner of the mutable task collection and move add, delete, mark, unmark, lookup, counting, and date-search operations behind its API. Rem now coordinates commands without manipulating the underlying ArrayList, while Storage receives a read-only snapshot for persistence.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align loading error with UI test
commitResults.messageBody: Replace the outdated loading-failure response with the message specified by TC-09. This keeps malformed saved data recoverable while making the fallback behavior clear and consistent with the documented console interface.

Add an abstract Command contract for execution and exit signaling, then move farewell behavior into ExitCommand. Routing only the bye case through the new hierarchy keeps this first stretch-goal increment small while establishing the pattern for later command extractions.

Move task listing and date-based schedule display into ListCommand and OnCommand. These commands share the new Command execution contract without requiring persistence, reducing the main switch while keeping mutation commands for later focused increments.

Move mark and unmark mutations, persistence, and result messages into MarkCommand and UnmarkCommand. Each command stores its validated task number, leaving Rem responsible only for parsing and dispatch during this incremental transition.

Move task removal, persistence, and remaining-count feedback into DeleteCommand. The command stores its validated task number, further reducing mutation-specific behavior in Rem while preserving the incremental dispatch structure.

Move task insertion, persistence, and count feedback into AddCommand. The command accepts an already-parsed Task, allowing todos, deadlines, and events to share one execution path without duplicating command classes.

Add a Parser factory that converts full user input into command objects and replace Rem's command switch with a generic parse, execute, and exit loop. The parser temporarily accepts the current task count so numbered-command validation remains behaviorally identical.

Convert Storage from a fixed static utility into an instance configured with a data-file path, then pass it through the Command execution contract. Mutation commands now persist through the supplied dependency, which makes storage ownership explicit and prepares Rem for constructor-based composition. Also include the previously verified TC-10 and TC-11 response corrections so the documented UI suite remains fully aligned.

Give Rem explicit Ui, Storage, and TaskList fields, load persisted tasks in its constructor, and move interaction into a reusable run method. Main now only constructs Rem with the default data path and starts it, matching the intended top-level OOP design.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move task range validation into TaskList
commitResults.messageBody: Let Parser construct numbered commands from syntax alone and defer task existence checks until execution. TaskList now validates mark, unmark, and delete numbers and reports the existing domain exception, allowing Rem to call Parser.parse with only the full user command.
Refresh task, schedule, and persistence responses to give Rem a more playful and consistent voice.
Point the application and shadow JAR settings at the packaged Rem entry point so the merged Gradle support runs the current application.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix visual bug regarding user's speech

commitResults.messageBody: Let users find tasks by a case-insensitive keyword while preserving task order. Validate missing keywords and cover the parser, task list, and console workflow with automated tests.
Use locale-independent case conversion so commands remain case-insensitive on systems such as Turkish locales. Add a regression test covering find recognition and deadline parsing.
